title: Mean spring timing correlation was positive but depended on the flow window at three Arctic gauges in 1980-2011
abstract: We tested shared spring flow timing at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka with ArcticGRO v20261104. We used 31 common complete certified years in 1980-2011, excluding 2000. After local linear trends were removed, the mean of three April-July midpoint correlations was 0.231. Conditional 95% five-year block limits were 0.081 to 0.406. Sixteen of 961 circular relative phase assignments had at least this mean. Pair correlations were -0.044, 0.368 and 0.370, so not all pairs moved together. Adding August reduced the mean to 0.064, with limits of -0.064 to 0.201. A contiguous 1980-1999 check was also uncertain. Thus the evidence depends on the flow window and sample. This extends earlier timing-trend and width tests with a shared annual timing statistic on the same source records. Short records, regulation, measurement error and approximate phase and block assumptions limit inference. The result does not establish a physical cause, a change in synchrony or simultaneous coastal freshwater delivery. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and reproduction instructions are supplied; source records and annual tables remain external.

display.caption: Local timing residuals, circular shift reference and planned window and sample checks. The positive main estimate weakens when August is included.
